data.title: XORTX Therapeutics Finalizes TSXV Delisting and Re-engages IR Agency in US$2.5 Million Nasdaq-Focused Campaign
data.description:
XORTX Therapeutics Inc ( (TSE:XRTX) ) has provided an announcement.

On August 28, 2026, XORTX Therapeutics received final approval to voluntarily delist its common shares from the TSX Venture Exchange, with the delisting taking effect after the close of business on September 1, 2026. The company’s shares continue to trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol XRTX, signaling a consolidation of its public-market presence in the United States.

The company had previously entered into an investor relations and marketing agreement with IR Agency LLC in May 2026, linked to a US$5 million public offering, but this original agreement was mutually terminated on August 7, 2026 and the full US$2.5 million fee was returned to XORTX on August 14, 2026. XORTX temporarily postponed its investor relations program during the delisting process and reserved the returned funds for future outreach initiatives.

Following completion of the TSXV delisting, XORTX re-engaged IR Agency under a revised consulting agreement signed on September 2, 2026, with services commencing September 3, 2026. The new agreement runs for three months, allows up to ten news distribution campaigns, and focuses on marketing and advertising services to communicate company information to the financial community.

Under the revised agreement, XORTX is paying IR Agency a US$2.5 million fee in advance, funded entirely from the previously returned amount and earmarked investor relations budget. The fee is fully earned upon receipt, non-refundable even if the contract is terminated, and either party retains the right to end the agreement at any time with written notice.

This sequence of delisting from the TSXV and restructured investor relations engagement reflects XORTX’s strategy to concentrate its capital markets activity around its Nasdaq listing while investing significantly in visibility among U.S. and global investors. For shareholders, the moves clarify the company’s market focus and indicate a planned, well-funded communications campaign aimed at supporting trading and awareness, albeit with no guarantees regarding market response or stock performance.

The events described occurred between May and early September 2026 and pertain to completed corporate actions, including the voluntary delisting and execution of the new consulting agreement. For market participants, these steps provide insight into XORTX’s evolving investor-relations approach and its broader positioning within the biopharmaceutical sector.

data.title: Virco Declares Q3 Dividend Amid Challenging Market Conditions
data.description:
Virco Manufacturing ( (VIRC) ) just unveiled an update.

Virco Mfg. Corporation, a leading U.S. manufacturer and direct supplier of movable furniture and equipment for educational environments and public spaces, reported weaker year-to-date financial results as the school furniture market continues to rebalance. The company nonetheless maintained strong gross margins and operating performance above long-term averages, supported by a domestically focused production model and a solid current ratio that underpins investment in existing and new revenue streams.

For the second quarter and six months ended July 31, 2026, Virco’s net sales declined to $87.5 million and $118.2 million respectively, down from $92.1 million and $125.8 million a year earlier, with operating income falling to $10.5 million for the quarter and $6.9 million year-to-date. Net income for the quarter dropped 15.4% to $8.6 million, and for the half fell 46.5% to $5.8 million, trends management attributes partly to budget uncertainties among public schools that tempered spending in the early part of the fiscal year.
